title: Database Formats and Multi-Contig Support
text: Starting misha 5.3.0, databases can stored two formats: Indexed format (default, recommended): Single unified files sequences tracks Per-chromosome format (legacy): Separate files chromosome indexed format provides better performance scalability, especially genomes many contigs (>50 chromosomes).

title: Database Formats and Multi-Contig Support
text: Automatic format detection - misha automatically detects format database uses Fully backward compatible - existing databases continue work without modification Transparent users - API formats Migration tools - convert databases convenient Performance benefits - 4-14% faster large-scale analyses

title: Database Formats and Multi-Contig Support
text: indexed format uses unified files: Sequence data: - seq/genome.seq - chromosome sequences concatenated - seq/genome.idx - Index mapping chromosome names positions Track data: - tracks/mytrack.track/track.dat - chromosome data concatenated - tracks/mytrack.track/track.idx - Index offset/length per chromosome Advantages: - Fewer file descriptors (important genomes 100+ contigs) - Better performance large workloads (14% faster) - Smaller disk footprint - Faster track creation conversion

title: Database Formats and Multi-Contig Support
text: per-chromosome format uses separate files: Sequence data: - seq/chr1.seq, seq/chr2.seq, … - One file per chromosome Track data: - tracks/mytrack.track/chr1.track, chr2.track, … - One file per chromosome use: - Compatibility older misha versions (<5.3.0) - Small genomes (<25 chromosomes) performance difference negligible

text: High priority (significant benefits): - Genomes many contigs (>50 chromosomes) - Large-scale analyses (10M+ bp regions frequently) - 2D track workflows - File descriptor limit issues Medium priority (moderate benefits): - Repeated extraction workflows - Regular analyses medium-sized regions (1-10M bp) Low priority (minimal benefits): - Small genomes (<25 chromosomes) - One-analyses - Simple queries small regions

text: Step 1: Backup (optional recommended) Step 2: Check current format Step 3: Convert Step 4: Verify Step 5: Remove backup (validation)

text: Exporting gextract(..., file = ...) re-importing gtrack.import() also works, lossy: binsize = 0 builds sparse track, dense source track comes back sparse 5x larger (20 bytes per value 4 bytes per bin). Reach destination misha database, actually want different track type.
code: gsetroot(source_db) exported <- file.path(tempdir(), "dense_track.txt") gextract("dense_track", gintervals.all(), iterator = "dense_track", file = exported)  gsetroot(target_db) gtrack.import("dense_track_roundtrip", "Round-tripped", exported, binsize = 0) gtrack.info("dense_track")[c("type", "size.in.bytes")] #> $type #> [1] "dense" #>  #> $size.in.bytes #> [1] 80012 gtrack.info("dense_track_roundtrip")[c("type", "size.in.bytes")] #> $type #> [1] "sparse" #>  #> $size.in.bytes #> [1] 400120 gtrack.rm("dense_track_roundtrip", force = TRUE)

text: UCSC mammal hubs host 224 241 Cactus / Zoonomia mammalian genomes uniform per-species directory layout, including chromAlias, repeat masker output, one GTFs per species. Build misha groot hub assembly : already private FASTA build accession (HAL- derived assembly) just want layer canonical annotations : groot built different chromosome-naming scheme hub uses (example, Cactus-derived names), hub’s chromAlias.txt consulted translate annotation chroms groot’s canonical names — strictly. chosen alias column must contain every groot chrom every distinct chrom source file; otherwise install errors diagnostic per-column overlap table. convert hub GTFs install needs UCSC’s gtfToGenePred binary (gff3ToGenePred NCBI Datasets sources). first call package prompts consent download UCSC’s prebuilt binaries (~5 MB ). pre-install non-interactive contexts: prebuilt binaries require glibc ≥ 2.34. older systems (e.g. CentOS 8) download succeed binary won’t run. Workaround: point misha env’s binaries:
code: # One-shot. Default sets = c("genes", "rmsk", "cgi", "cytoband"); cytoband and # (often) cgi are skipped with a warning since hubs don't ship them. gdb.build_genome("GCA_004023825.1",     path   = "/genomes/arctic_fox",     prefix = "intervs.global." ) gdb.install_intervals(     groot  = "/genomes/my_private_assembly",     source = list(source = "ucsc-hub", accession = "GCA_004023825.1"),     sets   = c("genes", "rmsk"),     prefix = "intervs.global." ) gdb.install_gff3_converter() gdb.install_gtf_converter() conda install -c bioconda ucsc-gff3togenepred ucsc-gtftogenepred Sys.setenv(MISHA_GFF3_TO_GENEPRED = "/path/to/env/bin/gff3ToGenePred") Sys.setenv(MISHA_GTF_TO_GENEPRED = "/path/to/env/bin/gtfToGenePred")

title: Manual
text: Dataset API distinguishes : Working Database: Set via gsetroot(), primary, writable database new tracks intervals created. Loaded Datasets: Added via gdataset.load(), read-data sources provide additional tracks intervals. Key Points: - sources must identical chrom_sizes.txt files (genome assembly) - working database used seq/ chrom_sizes.txt access - Tracks intervals aggregated sources - New tracks created working database
code: # The Dataset API needs more than one database. For this vignette the bundled # examples database is the working database, and a second, small database under # tempdir() plays the role of a shared, read-only annotation source. A dataset # only has to share the working database's chrom_sizes.txt. my_project <- .misha$GROOT shared_annotations <- file.path(tempdir(), "shared_annotations") unlink(shared_annotations, recursive = TRUE) dir.create(file.path(shared_annotations, "tracks"), recursive = TRUE) invisible(file.copy(file.path(my_project, "chrom_sizes.txt"), shared_annotations)) gtrack.copy("dense_track", "annotation_track", db = shared_annotations)  # Set your working database gsetroot(my_project)  # Load an additional dataset gdataset.load(shared_annotations)  # List all sources (working db + loaded datasets) gdataset.ls() #> [1] "/tmp/RtmphjRTkd/trackdb/test"       "/tmp/RtmphjRTkd/shared_annotations"  # Get detailed information gdataset.ls(dataframe = TRUE) #>                                 path tracks_total tracks_visible #> 1       /tmp/RtmphjRTkd/trackdb/test            5              5 #> 2 /tmp/RtmphjRTkd/shared_annotations            1              1 #>   intervals_total intervals_visible has_metadata writable #> 1               1                 1        FALSE     TRUE #> 2               0                 0        FALSE    FALSE

code: # A second dataset that also carries a track named "dense_track": other_dataset <- file.path(tempdir(), "other_dataset") unlink(other_dataset, recursive = TRUE) dir.create(file.path(other_dataset, "tracks"), recursive = TRUE) invisible(file.copy(file.path(my_project, "chrom_sizes.txt"), other_dataset)) gtrack.copy("dense_track", db = other_dataset)  gdataset.load(other_dataset) #> Error: #> ! Cannot load dataset '/tmp/RtmphjRTkd/other_dataset': #>   - tracks 'dense_track' already exist in working database '/tmp/RtmphjRTkd/trackdb/test' #> Use force=TRUE to override. # Working database always wins over datasets # (for dataset-to-dataset collisions, later-loaded wins) gdataset.load(other_dataset, force = TRUE)  # Check which source provides a track gtrack.dataset("dense_track") #> [1] "/tmp/RtmphjRTkd/trackdb/test"  # See all sources where a track exists (for debugging) gtrack.dbs("dense_track") #>                     dense_track                     dense_track  #>  "/tmp/RtmphjRTkd/trackdb/test" "/tmp/RtmphjRTkd/other_dataset"  gdataset.unload(other_dataset)

text: indexed format consolidates chromosome data two files: - track.dat: Single binary file containing concatenated track data chromosomes - track.idx: Binary index mapping chromosome IDs positions track.dat format dramatically reduces file descriptor usage genomes many contigs (e.g., draft assemblies thousands scaffolds) improves performance parallel access. Converting Indexed Format: Existing per-chromosome tracks can converted indexed format using gtrack.convert_to_indexed(): Supported Track Types: Dense (fixed-bin), Sparse, Array tracks (1D) Rectangles Points tracks (2D) can use indexed format. Virtual tracks Computed 2D tracks supported indexed format. Backward Compatibility: indexed format fully transparent misha functions. formats can coexist database used identically track expressions analysis functions. Validation Limits: prevent issues corrupted malicious index files, following limits enforced: Maximum contigs per index: 20,000,000 (applies genome.idx, track.idx, intervals.idx) Maximum contig name length: 1,024 bytes

text: Big interval sets can stored two formats: per-chromosome format indexed format. Per-Chromosome Format: traditional format, intervals chromosome (chromosome pair 2D intervals) stored separate files within interval set directory. 1D intervals: myintervals.interv/chr1, chr2, etc. 2D intervals: myintervals.interv/chr1-chr2, chr1-chr3, etc. Indexed Format (Recommended Multi-Contig Genomes): indexed format consolidates chromosomes two files, dramatically reducing file descriptor usage genomes many contigs. 1D Intervals use: - intervals.dat: Binary file concatenated interval data - intervals.idx: Binary index file (36-byte header + 24 bytes per contig) intervals.idx file structure: - Header (36 bytes): - Magic: "MISHAI1D" (8 bytes) - Version: uint32_t (4 bytes) - Number entries: uint32_t (4 bytes) - Flags: uint64_t (8 bytes) - bit 0 indicates little-endian - CRC64-ECMA checksum: uint64_t (8 bytes) - Reserved: uint32_t (4 bytes) Chromosome ID: uint32_t (4 bytes) Offset: uint64_t (8 bytes) Length: uint64_t (8 bytes) Reserved: uint32_t (4 bytes) 2D Intervals use: - intervals2d.dat: Binary file concatenated pair data - intervals2d.idx: Binary index file (40-byte header + 28 bytes per pair) intervals2d.idx file structure: - Header (40 bytes): - Magic: "MISHAI2D" (8 bytes) - Version: uint32_t (4 bytes) - Number entries: uint32_t (4 bytes) - Flags: uint64_t (8 bytes) - CRC64-ECMA checksum: uint64_t (8 bytes) - Reserved: uint64_t (8 bytes) Chromosome 1 ID: uint32_t (4 bytes) Chromosome 2 ID: uint32_t (4 bytes) Offset: uint64_t (8 bytes) Length: uint64_t (8 bytes) Reserved: uint32_t (4 bytes) Note: non-empty chromosome pairs stored 2D index, avoiding O(N²) space overhead. Converting Indexed Format: multi-byte integers stored little-endian byte order. indexed format fully backward compatible misha functions. text: addition using database tracks interval sets sources, virtual tracks can also use value-based tracks sources. Value-based tracks data frames containing genomic intervals associated numeric values. function -memory sparse tracks without requiring track creation database. create value-based virtual track, provide data frame columns chrom, start, end, one numeric value column (column name acceptable): Value-based tracks support track-based summarizer functions (e.g., avg, min, max, sum, stddev, quantile, nearest, exists, size, first, last, sample, position functions). However, one important restriction: intervals must overlap. Unlike interval-based summarizers (work overlapping intervals), value-based tracks behave like sparse tracks require non-overlapping intervals. Value-based tracks aggregate values using count-based averaging (interval contributes equally regardless length), matching behavior sparse tracks. means multiple intervals covered iterator interval, interval’s value contributes equally aggregation, regardless interval’s length. full list supported functions please see gvtrack.create gvtrack.array.slice functions.

title: Manual
text: misha package automatically configures based system’s resources loaded. happens transparently without user intervention: Automatic Process Limits: package detects number CPU cores sets gmax.processes = 70% cores. ensures optimal parallelism leaving headroom system. example: - 4-core laptop: gmax.processes = 2 (70% 4) - 16-core workstation: gmax.processes = 11 (70% 16) - 128-core server: gmax.processes = 89 (70% 128) Automatic Buffer Size: package coordinates buffer size process limits ensure gmax.processes * gmax.data.size <= 70% RAM. Specifically, sets gmax.data.size = min((RAM * 0.7) / gmax.processes, 10GB). ensures processes running full capacity, total memory usage stays within safe limits. example: - 4-core, 8GB laptop: gmax.processes = 2, gmax.data.size = 2.8GB (total: 5.6GB = 70% 8GB) - 16-core, 32GB workstation: gmax.processes = 11, gmax.data.size = 2.0GB (total: 22.4GB = 70% 32GB) - 128-core, 256GB server: gmax.processes = 89, gmax.data.size = 2.0GB (total: 179.2GB = 70% 256GB) 10GB cap empirically determined - larger shared memory allocations can fail even system limits appear allow . cap rarely hit multi-core systems due per-process division. Small Workloads: functions may choose run single-threaded small workloads avoid fork overhead. behavior can function-specific. disable multitasking entirely, set options(gmultitasking = FALSE). Manual Override: can still manually set options needed: check current auto-configured values:
code: options(gmax.processes = 32)        # Override process limit options(gmax.data.size = 5e9)       # Override buffer size (5GB) options(gmultitasking = FALSE)      # Disable multitasking entirely getOption("gmax.processes")         # Current process limit getOption("gmax.data.size") / 1e9   # Current buffer size in GB

code: library(misha) gdb.init_examples()  # 1) pick scope regions <- gintervals(1, 0, 50000)  # 2) inspect available tracks gtrack.ls() #> [1] "array_track"         "dense_track"         "rects_track"         #> [4] "sparse_track"        "subdir.dense_track2"  # 3) extract signal with a chosen iterator chip <- gextract("dense_track", regions, iterator = 100) head(chip) #>   chrom start end dense_track intervalID #> 1  chr1     0 100   0.1688889          1 #> 2  chr1   100 200   0.1700000          1 #> 3  chr1   200 300   0.1800000          1 #> 4  chr1   300 400   0.1600000          1 #> 5  chr1   400 500   0.1100000          1 #> 6  chr1   500 600   0.0400000          1  # 4) screen high-signal bins (as a simple peak-like filter). #    Pick the threshold from the data: dense_track only reaches 0.34 in this #    scope, so a threshold above that would silently screen nothing. hi_chip <- gscreen("dense_track > 0.2", regions, iterator = 100) head(hi_chip) #>   chrom start   end #> 1  chr1 17200 17300 #> 2  chr1 20000 20100 #> 3  chr1 23300 23400 #> 4  chr1 26200 26300 #> 5  chr1 32600 32800 #> 6  chr1 32900 33000  # 5) summarize distribution/coverage gsummary("dense_track", regions, iterator = 100) #> Total intervals   NaN intervals             Min             Max             Sum  #>    500.00000000      0.00000000      0.00000000      0.34000000     43.68888862  #>            Mean         Std dev  #>      0.08737778      0.06208607

text: Starting misha 4.2.0, package longer stores global variables ALLGENOME GROOT. code: ALLGENOME <<- .misha$ALLGENOME GROOT <<- .misha$GROOT ALLGENOME <<- .misha$ALLGENOME GINTERVID <<- .misha$GINTERVID GITERATOR.INTERVALS <<- .misha$GITERATOR.INTERVALS GROOT <<- .misha$GROOT GWD <<- .misha$GWD GTRACKS <<- .misha$GTRACKS

title: Change Database to Indexed Genome Format — gdb.convert_to_indexed
text: function converts per-chromosome database (separate .seq files per contig) indexed format (single genome.seq + genome.idx). indexed format provides better performance scalability, especially genomes many contigs. Important: Preserving Chromosome Order exact conversion produces bit--bit identical results conversion, load source database first using gsetroot() gdb.init(): database loaded: Uses chromosome order ALLGENOME (exact preservation) database loaded: Uses order chrom_sizes.txt (may differ ALLGENOME) ensures converted database exact chromosome ordering, affects iteration order, interval IDs, operations depend chromosome order. conversion process: Checks database already indexed format Gets chromosome order ALLGENOME (loaded) chrom_sizes.txt Consolidates per-chromosome .seq files genome.seq Creates genome.idx CRC64 checksum Optionally validates conversion Optionally removes old .seq files convert_tracks=TRUE, converts eligible tracks (1D: dense, sparse, array; 2D: rectangles, points) convert_intervals=TRUE, converts eligible interval sets (1D 2D) Tracks intervals converted (skipped): Tracks: virtual tracks, single-file tracks, already converted tracks Intervals: Single-file interval sets, already converted interval sets

title: Change Database to Indexed Genome Format — gdb.convert_to_indexed
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Recommended: Load database first for exact conversion gsetroot("/path/to/database") gdb.convert_to_indexed(     convert_tracks = TRUE,     convert_intervals = TRUE,     remove_old_files = TRUE,     verbose = TRUE )  # Convert current database to indexed format (genome only) gdb.convert_to_indexed()  # Convert specific database without loading it first # Note: chromosome order may differ from ALLGENOME gdb.convert_to_indexed(groot = "/path/to/database")  # Convert genome and all tracks to indexed format gdb.convert_to_indexed(convert_tracks = TRUE)  # Full conversion with validation and cleanup gsetroot("/path/to/database") # Load first for exact order preservation gdb.convert_to_indexed(     convert_tracks = TRUE,     convert_intervals = TRUE,     remove_old_files = TRUE,     validate = TRUE,     verbose = TRUE ) } # }

title: Install interval sets onto an existing groot — gdb.install_intervals
text: groot Path misha groot. NULL uses active groot. source Either registry name, recipe list, bare GC[FA]_<digits>.<digits> accession. sets Subset c("genes", "rmsk", "cgi", "cytoband"). prefix Character scalar prepended verbatim set name. Include trailing dot want one (e.g. "intervs.global."). gene_sets Named character vector mapping c("tss", "exons", "utr3", "utr5") -disk set name. NA value skips role. gtf_priority Character vector ordering GTF source preference sources ship multiple GTFs (currently ucsc-hub). First found wins. overwrite FALSE (default), error existing target sets. TRUE, remove existing sets saving. registry Optional path registry YAML; overrides resolution chain. target_chroms Optional character vector pin canonical column (e.g. chrom names halStats --sequenceStats HAL intend liftover ). NULL (default) misha uses groot's chrom names (.e. picks alias column matching whatever currently database). supplied, misha picks alias column matching target_chroms instead, switches detection count-weighted coverage (bp weighting requires lengths, target chrom lists typically carry). target_lengths Optional numeric vector aligned target_chroms. honored call originates gdb.build_genome (groot just force-aligned target_chroms); standalone calls ignore use strict column gate. honored, canonical set synthetic ".target_chroms" column populated name match + unique-length pairing, chrom_aliases.tsv writes target_chroms canonical chromAlias columns aliases. min_coverage Minimum fraction must covered chromAlias column picked canonical mapping. Default 1.0 (strict). groot side bp-weighted (fraction genome basepairs covered) - long-tail small unmapped contigs (e.g. 16 kb mitochondrion missing UCSC's genbank column 3 Gb genome) costs ~0.0005 (asset chroms read GTF/GFF) metric count-weighted fraction distinct names. Unmapped contigs receive annotations. match_by_length TRUE (default), complement column-based canonical detection per-row length-based fill: alias rows whose chosen column empty paired groot chrom length, length unique sides (ambiguous lengths skipped, never guessed). Asset translation also switches per-row cross-column lookup, GFF naming scheme (mixed schemes) imports cleanly. Currently honored ucsc-hub backend (ships per-contig lengths <acc>.chrom.sizes.txt); backends unaffected. Set FALSE stricter single-column-behavior. force FALSE (default), requested set source provide raises error aborts call touching groot. TRUE, missing sets demoted single summary warning available sets installed. verbose TRUE, prints progress. prefetched_alias Optional pre-fetched chromAlias bundle (return value .hub_preflight_coverage). supplied ucsc-hub fetcher reuses instead re-downloading. Internal; users never set directly. .from_build_genome Internal flag; TRUE, gdb.build_genome signals already rescanned groot can skip entry rescan. Users never set directly.

title: Annotates 1D intervals using nearest neighbors — gintervals.annotate
code: # Prepare toy data intervs <- gintervals(1, c(1000, 5000), c(1100, 5050)) ann <- gintervals(1, c(900, 5400), c(950, 5500)) ann$remark <- c("a", "b") ann$score <- c(10, 20)  # Basic usage with default columns (all non-basic columns) gintervals.annotate(intervs, ann) #>   chrom start  end remark score dist #> 1  chr1  1000 1100      a    10   50 #> 2  chr1  5000 5050      b    20  350  # Select specific columns, with custom names and distance column name gintervals.annotate(     intervs, ann,     annotation_columns = c("remark"),     column_names = c("ann_remark"),     dist_column = "ann_dist" ) #>   chrom start  end ann_remark ann_dist #> 1  chr1  1000 1100          a       50 #> 2  chr1  5000 5050          b      350  # Distance threshold with scalar NA replacement gintervals.annotate(     intervs, ann,     annotation_columns = c("remark"),     max_dist = 200,     na_value = "no_ann" ) #>   chrom start  end remark dist #> 1  chr1  1000 1100      a   50 #> 2  chr1  5000 5050 no_ann  350  # Multiple neighbors with deterministic tie-breaking nbrs <- gintervals.annotate(     gintervals(1, 1000, 1100),     {         x <- gintervals(1, c(800, 1200), c(900, 1300))         x$label <- c("left", "right")         x     },     annotation_columns = "label",     maxneighbors = 2,     tie_method = "min.start" ) nbrs #>   chrom start  end label dist #> 1  chr1  1000 1100  left  100 #> 2  chr1  1000 1100 right  100  # Overwrite existing columns in the base intervals intervs2 <- intervs intervs2$remark <- c("orig1", "orig2") gintervals.annotate(intervs2, ann, annotation_columns = "remark", overwrite = TRUE) #>   chrom start  end remark dist #> 1  chr1  1000 1100      a   50 #> 2  chr1  5000 5050      b  350

title: Converts intervals to canonic form — gintervals.canonic
code: gdb.init_examples()  ## Create intervals manually by using 'data.frame'. ## Note that we add an additional column 'data'. ## Return value: ##   chrom start   end data ## 1  chr1 11000 12000   10 ## 2  chr1   100   200   20 ## 3  chr1 10000 13000   30 ## 4  chr1 10500 10600   40 intervs <- data.frame(     chrom = "chr1",     start = c(11000, 100, 10000, 10500),     end = c(12000, 200, 13000, 10600),     data = c(10, 20, 30, 40) )  ## Convert the intervals into the canonic form. ## The function discards any columns besides chrom, start and end. ## Return value: ##  chrom start   end ## 1  chr1   100   200 ## 2  chr1 10000 13000 res <- gintervals.canonic(intervs)  ## By inspecting mapping attribute we can see how the new ## intervals were created: "2 1 2 2" means that the first ## interval in the result was created from the second interval in ## the original set (we look for the indices in mapping where "1" ## appears). Likewise the second interval in the result was ## created from 3 intervals in the original set. Their indices are ## 1, 3 and 4 (once again we look for the indices in mapping where ## "2" appears). ## Return value: ## 2 1 2 2 attr(res, "mapping") #> [1] 2 1 2 2  ## Finally (and that is the most useful part of 'mapping' ## attribute): we add a new column 'data' to our result which is ## the mean value of the original data column. The trick is done ## using 'tapply' on par with 'mapping' attribute. For example, ## 20.00000 equals is a result of 'mean(intervs[2,]$data' while ## 26.66667 is a result of 'mean(intervs[c(1,3,4),]$data)'. ## 'res' after the following call: ##  chrom start   end     data ## 1  chr1   100   200 20.00000 ## 2  chr1 10000 13000 26.66667 res$data <- tapply(intervs$data, attr(res, "mapping"), mean)

title: Score DNA sequences with a PWM over a region of interest — gseq.pwm
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Create a PSSM (position-specific scoring matrix) with frequency values pssm <- matrix(     c(         0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1, # Position 1: mostly A         0.1, 0.7, 0.1, 0.1, # Position 2: mostly C         0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.1, # Position 3: mostly G         0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7 # Position 4: mostly T     ),     ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE ) colnames(pssm) <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")  # Example sequences seqs <- c("ACGTACGTACGT", "GGGGACGTCCCC", "TTTTTTTTTTT")  # Score sequences using log-sum-exp (default mode) gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "lse")  # Get maximum score gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "max")  # Find position of best match gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "pos")  # Find position with strand information gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "pos", bidirect = TRUE, return_strand = TRUE)  # Count matches above threshold. score.thresh is mandatory in "count" mode # and has no default: PWM scores are log-likelihoods, so calibrate it # against the score range of your own PSSM. range(gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "max")) gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "count", score.thresh = -3)  # Score only a region of interest gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "max", start_pos = 3, end_pos = 10)  # Allow matches to extend beyond ROI boundaries gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "count", score.thresh = -3, start_pos = 5, end_pos = 8, extend = TRUE)  # Spatial weighting example: higher weight in the center spatial_weights <- c(0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 0.5) gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm,     mode = "lse",     spat.factor = spatial_weights,     spat.bin = 2 ) } # }

title: Forbid a k-mer pattern in a trained gsynth model — gsynth.forbid_kmer
text: Useful building CpG-null, motif-null, repeat-class-null synthetic backgrounds standard gsynth.train() model without retraining. Seeding caveat. gsynth.sample initializes first k bases sampling interval uniform random draw, seed bases may contain pattern. seed lands state k-mer already contains pattern substring, every possible next base extend occurrence thus forbidden; "trapped" states fall back uniform sampling (forbid'd CDF) pattern slides state window. guarantee applies Markov-sampled bases downstream trap-escape window, first bases interval. Expected residual per interval small nonzero; strict pattern-free output, pass mask_copy gsynth.sample seed known pattern-free reference, scrub residuals sampling.

title: Creates a track from WIG / BigWig / BedGraph / BED / tab-delimited file — gtrack.import
text: function creates track WIG / BigWig / BedGraph / tab-delimited file. Zipped files supported (file name must '.gz' '.zip' suffix). Tab-delimited files must start header line following column names (tab-separated): 'chrom', 'start', 'end', exactly one value column name (e.g. 'value'). subsequent line provides single interval: - chrom: chromosome name (e.g. 'chr1') - start: 0-based start coordinate (inclusive) - end: 0-based end coordinate (exclusive) - value: numeric value (floating point allowed); exactly one value column supported Columns must separated tabs. Coordinates must refer chromosomes existing current genome. Missing values can specified 'NaN'. Chromosome names matched genome database chromosome alias chain (chr1 <-> 1, M <-> MT, <groot>/chrom_aliases.tsv present). file names chromosomes none can matched, 'gtrack.import' fails instead creating empty track; file chromosome records error still imports empty track. names can matched, rest file imported unmatched names reported: message contigs database (unplaced scaffolds, patches), warning unmatched name looks like primary chromosome, since suggests naming mismatch. BED files (.bed/.bed.gz/.bed.zip) also supported. BED 'score' column (5th column) exists numeric, used interval value; otherwise constant value 1 used. BED inputs, 'binsize' controls output type: 'binsize' 0 track 'Sparse'; otherwise track 'Dense' bin-averaged values based overlaps BED intervals ('defval' regions covered). 'binsize' 0 resulted track created 'Sparse' format. Otherwise 'Dense' format chosen bin size equal 'binsize'. values defined input file file substituted 'defval' value. 'description' added track attribute. multiple databases connected via gsetroot, track created current working directory (.misha$GWD), defaults last connected database. Use gdir.cd absolute path change new tracks created.

title: Creates a track from WIG / BigWig / BedGraph / BED / tab-delimited file — gtrack.import
code: # \donttest{ gdb.init_examples()  # Create a simple WIG file for demonstration temp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".wig") writeLines(c(     "track type=wiggle_0 name=\"example track\"",     "fixedStep chrom=chr1 start=1 step=1",     "1.5",     "2.0",     "1.8",     "3.2" ), temp_file)  # Basic import gtrack.import("example_track", "Example track from WIG file",     temp_file,     binsize = 1 ) gtrack.info("example_track") #> $type #> [1] "dense" #>  #> $dimensions #> [1] 1 #>  #> $size.in.bytes #> [1] 4000012 #>  #> $format #> [1] "per-chromosome" #>  #> $bin.size #> [1] 1 #>  gtrack.rm("example_track", force = TRUE)  # Import with custom attributes attrs <- c("author" = "researcher", "version" = "1.0", "experiment" = "test") gtrack.import("example_track_with_attrs", "Example track with attributes",     temp_file,     binsize = 1, attrs = attrs )  # Check that attributes were set gtrack.attr.get("example_track_with_attrs", "author") #> [1] "researcher" gtrack.attr.get("example_track_with_attrs", "version") #> [1] "1.0" gtrack.attr.get("example_track_with_attrs", "experiment") #> [1] "test"  # Clean up gtrack.rm("example_track_with_attrs", force = TRUE) # }

code: gdb.init_examples()  ## Basic usage: Excluding specific regions gvtrack.create("vtrack1", "dense_track", func = "avg")  # Create intervals to mask (e.g., repetitive regions) repeats <- gintervals(c(1, 1), c(100, 500), c(200, 600))  # Attach filter - track will be evaluated excluding these regions gvtrack.filter("vtrack1", filter = repeats)  # Extract values - masked regions are excluded from calculation result_filtered <- gextract("vtrack1", gintervals(1, 0, 1000))  # Check filter info gvtrack.info("vtrack1") #> $src #> [1] "dense_track" #>  #> $func #> [1] "avg" #>  #> $filter #> [1] "filter__tmp_RtmpnFDIjp_trackdb_test_tracks_2_7d54e8370e6eb979" #>  #> $filter_stats #> $filter_stats$num_chroms #> [1] 1 #>  #> $filter_stats$total_bases #> [1] 200 #>  #> $filter_stats$empty #> [1] FALSE #>  #>   # Clear the filter and compare gvtrack.filter("vtrack1", filter = NULL) result_unfiltered <- gextract("vtrack1", gintervals(1, 0, 1000))  ## Using multiple filter sources (combined automatically) centromeres <- gintervals(1, 10000, 15000) telomeres <- gintervals(1, 0, 1000) combined_mask <- list(repeats, centromeres, telomeres)  gvtrack.filter("vtrack1", filter = combined_mask) result_multi_filter <- gextract("vtrack1", gintervals(1, 0, 20000))  ## Filters work with iterator modifiers gvtrack.create("vtrack2", "dense_track", func = "sum") gvtrack.filter("vtrack2", filter = repeats) gvtrack.iterator("vtrack2", sshift = -50, eshift = 50)  # Iterator shifts applied first, then mask subtracted result_shifted <- gextract("vtrack2", gintervals(1, 1000, 2000), iterator = 100)

Behavior fix: gintervals.annotate() fills na_value query intervals neighbor range (previously left NA). gtrack.convert() explicit target track now registers new track (previously unusable, trashed indexed database, reload). gtrack.import_set() derives track name file name ; dot parent directory longer truncates (silently collided imports). gtrack.ls(db=...) returns tracks one database loaded (previously NULL). gtrack.var.ls() accepts expression (e.g. tracks[]) track argument, like gtrack.var.get/set/rm. gsetroot() leaves current database loaded target’s chrom_sizes.txt missing malformed (previously unloaded session first). Fixed --bounds memory accesses gintervals.liftover() aggregation, strand-autocorrelation reads near contig ends, indexed fixed-bin track validation; clearer “data size exceeded” message. Non-ASCII track attribute values longer truncate read back. gtrack.array.extract() rejects NA column indices instead forwarding . Fixed 2D indexed-format writer produced unreadable interval sets options(gmulticontig.indexed_format = TRUE). created.provenance strings gtrack.2d.create(), gtrack.2d.import_contacts(), gtrack.modify() now well-formed. gmax.processes floored 1 (0 single-core / undetectable-core hosts). Internal hardening: ggenome.implant() longer leaks buffers error paths; corrupt-file checks -disk 2D quadtree.

title: misha 5.11.8
text: Behavior fix: 2D gtrack.liftover() now aggregates overlapping mapped rectangles instead inserting overlapping objects (corrupted read-back double-counted). multi_target_agg, na.rm, min_n now apply 2D tracks , matching 1D path. Overlaps arise chain maps disjoint source rectangles onto overlapping target rectangles; lifted 2D track values change accordingly.

title: misha 5.11.7
text: Behavior fix: gintervals.liftover() longer silently drops interval whose start coincides leftmost overlapping chain lifted call wider interval (map_interval slow-path miss; carried hint advanced past chain). Affected multi-interval lifts target policy. gtrack.liftover() now rejects cluster target-overlap policies (best_source_cluster, best_cluster_union, best_cluster_sum, best_cluster_max) clear error - implemented gintervals.liftover(); previously failed confusing internal message.

title: misha 5.11.6
text: Behavior fix: gtrack.liftover() aggregation (multi_target_agg) now combines distinct source bins map target bin, instead keeping first several come chain. Previously, chain whose blocks aligned bin grid (.e. real liftovers), max/sum/mean/count reflected first contributing source bin. (gintervals.liftover already correct.) Lifted track values change accordingly.

title: misha 5.11.5
text: Behavior fix: gtrack.liftover() / gintervals.liftover() minus-strand chain target-overlap sweep truncates splits (e.g. tgt_overlap_policy = "auto") now keep correct reversed source coordinates surviving slice instead coordinates discarded half. Behavior fix: gtrack.liftover() / gintervals.liftover() longer drop chain’s finite contribution target locus chain also maps NaN source bin na.rm = TRUE; NaN pieces now removed per-chain merge. Behavior fix: 2D gtrack.liftover() longer drops rectangles chain multiple blocks (quadtree’s spatial iteration order defeated carried mapping cursor).

title: misha 5.11.4
text: Behavior fix: gintervals.liftover() / gtrack.liftover() longer drop mapping wider earlier source chain source chains overlap (src_overlap_policy = "keep"). map_interval fast path trusted carried cursor leftmost overlap checking immediate predecessor; now confirms leftmost-ness via per-chromosome prefix-max, falling back full search otherwise.

title: misha 5.11.3
text: Behavior fix: gtrack.liftover(tgt_overlap_policy = "agg") longer drops lifted contribution spans target bin boundary overlapping chain shares interval. per-bin sweep -advanced cursor, losing spanning contribution next bin producing spurious NaNs (wrong aggregates) bins fed multiple overlapping chains.

title: misha 5.11.2
text: Behavior fix: gintervals.load_chain(..., src_groot=) longer leaves session pointing source database validation. now fully restores active database - working directory (GWD), loaded datasets virtual tracks included, just genome root.

title: misha 5.11.1
text: Behavior fix: gquantiles() / gintervals.quantiles() name percentile columns shortest decimal round-trips percentile, nearby percentiles longer collapse name - e.g. 0.123456789 0.1234567891 previously became "0.123457", 0.9999999 became "1" (colliding 1.0 quantile). Common percentiles (0.5, 0.95, …) unchanged.

title: misha 5.11.0
text: Breaking: gextract() longer truncates auto-generated column names 40 characters - columns named full expression (complete track name) instead <first 37 chars>.... Long names previously collapsed truncated name, hiding column, now distinct. Pass colnames= set names explicitly.

title: misha 5.10.3
text: Behavior fix: reading indexed dense track empty (length-0) contig follows populated one scan longer returns previous chromosome’s values. mmap read path (added 5.6.7) left window pointing prior chrom length-0 entry, max.pos.*/min.pos.*, mixed-function, avg+nearest virtual tracks read stale values empty contig instead NA. Single-function avg/sum/lse tracks unaffected. Behavior fix: pwm.edit_distance / pwm.edit_distance.pos / pwm.max.edit_distance direction = "" max_edits set longer skip N-containing windows. N mandatory edit going threshold, N-heavy window already scoring threshold needs 0 edits; N-count skip (added 5.6.11) wrongly pruned windows, returning NA missing true minimum. skip now restricted direction = "" substitutions-, exact.

title: misha 5.10.2
text: Performance fix: single-function lse (sum/exists/size) virtual track scanned sliding window (gvtrack.iterator(sshift=, eshift=)) genome-wide fast . Since 5.6.7 single-function “fast path” recomputed windowed reduction scratch every step, bypassing incremental sliding-window path; common motif-energy quantile workload (windowed lse + gquantiles/gscreen) ~2.5x slower (worse wider windows). single-function reducers now keep sliding-window path. Output unchanged.

title: misha 5.10.1
text: Behavior fix: indexed dense tracks whose first genome chrom data (typically produced gtrack.copy() destination DB leading chrom source’s per-chrom files) longer report bin.size = 0 gtrack.info() longer SIGFPE subsequent reads. GenomeTrackFixedBin::init_read now back-fills m_bin_size first non-empty index entry length-0 lookup, instead leaving constructor default. Behavior fix: gtrack.info() per-chromosome dense track whose first genome chrom per-chrom file (empty scaffold, partial track) now reports correct bin.size instead erroring “file directory”. also unblocks gtrack.copy() tracks, calls gtrack.info() source.

title: misha 5.10.0
text: gdb.install_intervals() / gdb.build_genome() now attach name (transcript accession) geneName (gene symbol) columns installed tss/exons/utr3/utr5 sets, taken source annotation. Sources without symbols build cleanly blank geneName.

title: misha 5.9.1
text: Behavior fix: distance, distance.edge, distance.center virtual-track functions now always return true nearest source interval. overlapping nested sources (e.g. intervs.global.rmsk) old scan return non-nearest interval - even nonzero distance query overlaps source. distance.edge matches gintervals.neighbors exactly. distance.center now accepts overlapping source intervals (query center inside several resolves nearest center) instead erroring vtrack creation.

title: misha 5.9.0
text: gintervals.2d.intersect() gintervals.2d.union() general 2D (rectangle) interval set operations, complementing existing gintervals.2d.band_intersect(). Intersection clips overlapping rectangles pairwise per chromosome pair; union concatenates without merging (union two rectangles rectangle). gintervals.from_strings() builds 1D intervals UCSC-style coordinate strings "chr1:1000-2000" (optional :+/:- strand; bare "chr1" whole chromosome). gvtrack.clear() removes virtual tracks current working directory one call. gdb.unload() unloads active genome database resets session uninitialized state.

title: misha 5.8.1
text: gtrack.import_mappedseq() strand-autocorrelation importer now print correct message (instead garbage value possible crash) given non-positive cols.order entry; latter also reports offending maxread rather binsize. ggenome.implant() validates output trackdb destination writing FASTA, pre-existing trackdb overwrite = FALSE longer leaves orphaned output file behind.

title: misha 5.8.1
text: gintervals.force_range() markedly faster writing output set (big-set inputs) genomes many contigs: per-chromosome chromosome-end lookup computed instead re-derived full genome every chromosome.

title: misha 5.8.0
text: gtrack.import_mappedseq() now accepts BAM files directly: bgzip magic bytes auto-detected file streamed samtools view existing parser. Requires samtools PATH (declared SystemRequirements); clear error names missing tool otherwise. BAM input function treats default cols.order = c(9, 11, 13, 14) SAM mode (.e. NULL); explicitly passing non-NULL cols.order BAM file rejected error. gtrack.import_mappedseq() also auto-detects plain gzipped SAM / TSV input (.sam.gz, .tsv.gz) via zlib. user-facing API change. Progress reporting now caps 100% (previously overshoot iterator step budgets -estimated).

title: misha 5.7.4
text: Behavior fix: gintervals.load() 1D/2D big intervals set whose meta-stats exactly one row returning wrong slice (typo meta$stat -> meta$stats). Behavior fix: gtracksummary() / gintervals.summary() standard deviation now returns 0 instead NaN nearly-constant input; catastrophic-cancellation clamp applied Spearman correlation. Behavior fix: gtrack.rm() / gintervals.rm() / gdir.rm() non-interactive session without force = TRUE now stop clear message instead crashing readLines(n = 1) returning length-zero. Behavior fix: gsynth.random() rejects nuc_probs duplicated missing names (previously silently produced NaN probabilities). gtrack.import() accepts bedGraph genomes whose contig names don’t start chr (Ensembl-style, non-mammalian, scaffolded contigs). Plugged FILE-handle leaks exception paths big-intervals readers, RSaneSerialize/RSaneUnserialize, Computer2D::unserializeComputer2D. Numerous correctness fixes error messages (typos, missing sprintf args, broken format specifiers) defensive emptiness handling (1:length() / 1:nrow() -> seq_along() / seq_len()).

title: misha 5.7.4
text: Removed O(N²) per-chromosome accumulator patterns .gintervals.apply gintervals FUN closures (gintervals.diff / .intersect / .union / .canonic / .normalize / .rbind / .neighbors / gintervals.mapply). ~70× speedup 5000+ chromosomes; previously catastrophic million-contig scHi-C-scaffolded genomes. gseq.pwm_edits() chromosome-boundary clamp vectorized: O(N) instead O(N · scaffolds).

title: misha 5.7.3
text: gdb.reload() now also clears C++ track-index cache, track replaced --process (sibling R session, manual rebuild another script) picked running session without restarting R. Previously cached track type shadow new -disk track surface e.g. function global.percentile.max supported sparse tracks track already rebuilt dense.

title: misha 5.7.2
text: gtrack.import() malformed WIG/CSV file now surfaces underlying parser error (file name, line number, wrong) instead opaque Unrecognized format file .... Makes typical failure modes (e.g. value line glued fixedStep header botched cat-style concatenation) diagnosable glance.

title: misha 5.7.1
text: gextract() gains intervals_join argument values "id" (default; current behavior), "intervals" (drop intervalID, attach input intervals data frame’s columns output row), "none" (drop intervalID). Built-replacement misha.ext::gextract.left_join, around 2x faster wide-window workloads (e.g. TSS +/- 5kb 50bp iterator). Fixed gtrack.import() BED files binsize failing func argument string. BED--dense path updated gtrack.create_dense() gained func argument 5.6.31; now passes historical "weighted.mean" default.

title: misha 5.6.33
text: Track-creation writes (gtrack.create_sparse(), gtrack.create_dense(), gtrack.create(), gtrack.smooth(), gtrack.modify(), gtrack.convert_to_indexed()) coalesce far fewer syscalls networked filesystems bumping stdio buffer 1 MiB every misha-managed write file. Noticeable NFS-mounted track DBs. gtrack.create_sparse() per-chromosome (non-indexed) DBs now creates empty-chrom signature files parallel via raw POSIX syscalls. Worker count configurable via gtrack.create.threads option (default 4, matching NFSv3 CREATE concurrency).

title: misha 5.6.33
text: Behavior fix: gtrack.rm("X") followed gtrack.create_*("X", ...) (analogous gintervals.rm + gintervals.save cycle) indexed DB longer breaks subsequent reads. process-static index caches keyed track/intervals directory path never invalidated, rm--recreate readers route stale layout error open track.dat: file directory silently return data prior lifecycle. Latent since v5.1.1 (1D tracks interval sets) v5.5.0 (2D tracks).

title: misha 5.6.32
text: Fixed gtrack.create_dense() returning wrong values (func = "coverage" exploding huge numbers) overlapping intervals mixed lengths fed bin. Older callers using default func = "weighted.mean" got plausible-looking algebraically wrong means affected bins. Additional cache-protection fixes covering tracks intervals path lookups; closes remaining -family GC-safety gaps 5.6.31 chromkey fix.

title: misha 5.6.31
text: gtrack.create_dense() gains func argument selecting per-bin aggregation overlapping intervals: "weighted.mean" (default, unchanged ), "weighted.sum", "max", "min", "median", "count", "coverage" (= sum(v_i * ov_i) / binsize, .e. average per-base signal; values = rep(1, n) ChIP-seq-style pileup track one call). Fixed crashes calling misha functions gdb.init_examples() R installations. gdb.install_intervals(..., sets = "genes") NCBI longer aborts handful unconvertible GFF records (typically immunoglobulin loci RefSeq human/mouse): gff3ToGenePred now invoked -warnAndContinue, offending transcripts skipped warning rest genome installed.

title: misha 5.6.30
text: gtrack.rm() (gintervals.rm()) now returns immediately even target directory contains millions files; actual filesystem cleanup runs background. Track creation (gtrack.create() friends) now atomic databases many contigs: interrupted create longer leaves partial track directory blocks re-creation. Cleanup failed creates runs background. indexed databases, gtrack.create() dense (fixed-bin) sparse tracks now writes indexed format (track.dat + track.idx) directly instead writing N per-chromosome files deleting . Substantially faster databases >1M contigs. 2D track / interval-set creation meta builders longer allocate O(num_contigs^2) per-pair entries. gtrack.create_meta() 2D tracks uses track.idx (indexed) directory scan (legacy) enumerate populated pairs instead probing N*N. Enables 2D tracks databases >1000 contigs without OOM multi-day metadata scans. gdataset.info() gdataset.ls(dataframe=TRUE) now use single C++ filesystem traversal (FTS_SKIP) instead two recursive R-level list.files() calls. Faster databases many tracks/intervals .db.cache missing stale. gtrack.liftover() now writes indexed format directly target database indexed, avoiding ~1M per-chromosome empty-placeholder file creations lifting onto many-contig genome. gdb.convert_to_indexed(convert_tracks = TRUE) convert_intervals = TRUE accept new threads argument (default: min(detectCores(), 8)) run per-track conversions parallel via parallel::mclapply. Per-track failures reported warnings without aborting batch. gtrack.create_meta() sparse/array tracks indexed databases now consults track.idx find populated chromosomes instead stat’ing per-chromosome files don’t exist. Drops one-time O(N_contigs) syscall cost first use sparse/array track. gextract() / gscreen() track-expression iterators now validate indexed 1D tracks via track.idx instead stat’ing per chromosome. 1.28M-contig database, gextract 100 random 5 bp intervals dense indexed track drops ~64 s ~8 s (system time ~52 s ~2 s). Fixed gintervals.random() rejecting chromosomes whose length exactly equals size + 2*dist_from_edge (single valid interval available) biasing sampling away right edge. -filter path now uses full-range semantics filter path. misha functions paid fixed ~1.5 s setup cost million-contig databases (rebuilding chromosome table -genome interval list every call). now cached. 1.28M-contig database, gtrack.info() drops ~1.4 s <1 ms gseq.extract() ~14 s ~0.4 s; smaller genomes unaffected. gsetroot() ~3x faster million-contig databases (~13 s -> ~5 s 1.28M-contig DB). gextract() scan operations faster indexed tracks databases many chromosome aliases (skips per-contig alias lookup effect indexed tracks). gdb.install_intervals() ncbi now translates chrom names groot’s convention, fetches genes rmsk NCBI FTP Datasets API doesn’t ship (older / suppressed accessions like GRCm38.p6), longer downloads FASTA. min_coverage now checked alias rescue passes, hybrid naming (e.g. UCSC-style chroms mixed bare GenBank accessions) passes strict default.

title: misha 5.6.29
text: gdb.install_intervals() now errors requested set unavailable source (previously skipped silently warning). Pass force = TRUE demote error summary warning install available sets.

title: misha 5.6.28
text: gtrack.copy() gained db argument copy tracks across databases, overwrite argument replace existing destinations. Format conversion (per-chromosome <-> indexed) chromosome-order remap handled automatically. Multi-track input also supported.

title: misha 5.6.27
text: Added gdb.build_genome(name) build--source genome creation. Backends: ucsc (golden path), ucsc-hub (224/241 Zoonomia mammals), ncbi (Datasets API), manual, local, s3. name resolves registry chain (misha.genome_registry option, project-local misha.yaml, built-inst/genomes.yaml), fallback ucsc-hub GC[FA]_* accessions. Companions: gdb.list_genomes(), gdb.genome_info(). Added gdb.install_intervals() layer gene / rmsk / cgi / cytoband sets onto existing groot - useful adding annotations private FASTA build resuming failed install without re-fetching. rmsk now also produces per-class subsets rmsk_<class> (e.g. rmsk_sine). Naming alignment external schemes (e.g. HAL canonical names) via target_chroms / target_lengths / match_by_length (default TRUE) / chrom_naming / min_coverage arguments: misha picks chromAlias column best matches target falls back per-row length pairing single column doesn’t cover everything. UCSC-hub builds also merge <acc>_assembly_report.txt present expose extra alias columns. Coverage bp-weighted groot side, small unmapped contigs (e.g. 16 kb mitochondrion) don’t trip thresholds. Cheap pre-flight runs multi-GB download: UCSC-hub coverage checked ~190 KB metadata; NCBI annotation availability checked via Datasets dataset_report. Missing-annotation builds drop genes actionable warning (suggesting RefSeq companion one exists). Post-pre-flight failures clean partial output directory. Added gdb.install_gff3_converter() / gdb.install_gtf_converter() pre-install UCSC gff3ToGenePred / gtfToGenePred binaries; override paths via MISHA_GFF3_TO_GENEPRED / MISHA_GTF_TO_GENEPRED. UCSC’s prebuilt binaries need glibc >= 2.34; older systems can conda install -c bioconda ucsc-gff3togenepred ucsc-gtftogenepred. Renames gdb.build_genome(): argument annotations -> sets; track cpgIsland -> cgi. gsetroot much faster fragmented assemblies (e.g. ~93 s -> ~11 s 2.4M-contig genome). gdb.build_genome() gdb.install_intervals() also substantially faster large assemblies (vectorized chromAlias translation RepeatMasker .parsing, optional data.table genePred /O).

title: misha 5.6.26
text: Fixed gpartition, gquantiles consumers BinFinder silently routing every value highest bin breaks vector contained -Inf +Inf (e.g. c(-Inf, 0, Inf)). uniform-binsize fast path computed Inf/Inf = NaN whose cast int undefined behaviour. BinFinder::init now falls back binary search binsize non-finite.

title: misha 5.6.25
text: gsynth.sample() gsynth.random() now preserve N (lowercase n) positions original reference default. Previously, every position filled sampled/random ACGT base, reference gaps centromeres came fabricated nucleotides. Pass preserve_n = FALSE restore legacy behavior.

title: misha 5.6.24
text: Fixed gquantiles (gmultitasking = FALSE) hanging hours first global.percentile.max lookup fresh dense track (regression 5.6.20 single-process fast path). ~2*log_2(N) target ranks fast path now sorts reservoir indexes; suffix walk preserved. Single-process multitask results remain bit-identical. Fixed small-scope gscreen regression introduced 5.6.7 sub-chromosome range splitting: iterator=1 ~5 Mb scope, range-split forks small amortise fork overhead. Added 500 kbp-per-kid floor; full-genome scans still cap gmax.processes kids. Measured chr19:0-5 Mb gscreen: 1.47 s -> 0.31 s.

title: misha 5.6.23
text: Improved error messages: “start exceeds equals end” now mentions misha’s 0-based half-open convention GFF/VCF 1-based hint; “chromosome exist” lists known chromosomes points CHROM_ALIAS. C++ converter now emits R warning (“N intervals start == end extended 1bp”) zero-length intervals loaded file auto-bumped (previously silent). Added gintervals.import_bed(), gintervals.import_gff(), gintervals.import_vcf() direct import common interval file formats. three normalize chromosome names via CHROM_ALIAS, apply misha’s 0-based half-open convention (subtracting 1 start 1-based GFF/GTF/VCF inputs), preserve common metadata columns (name/score/strand BED; type/source/score/attrs GFF; id/ref/alt/qual/filter/info VCF).

title: misha 5.6.22
text: Intervals’ strand column now accepts character ("+", "-", ".", "*", "") factor input addition numeric 1/-1/0. Strings normalized numeric convention R->C++ boundary; output stays numeric.

title: misha 5.6.21
text: Added prior argument gsynth.train() (default "marginal"). Per-bin Dirichlet priors now learned trainer’s counts default, unobserved (cell, k-mer-context) entries fall back cell’s empirical base composition instead uniform 1/4. modes: "global", NULL/"uniform", length-4 numeric, n_bins x 4 matrix. CDF formula changed (N + alpha) / (sum_a N + 4*alpha) (N + alpha * pi_a(b)) / (sum_a N + alpha) (pi sums 1). reproduce pre-5.6.21 Laplace-add-one behavior, pass prior = NULL, pseudocount = 4. .gsm metadata gains optional prior/prior_mode fields; older files load prior = uniform (-disk CDF truth).

title: misha 5.6.20
text: Fixed gquantiles hanging many minutes dense binsize=1 whole-genome scans. Kids now sort samples buffer packing parent heap-based k-way merge instead global single-thread sort; single-process path uses std::nth_element per percentile rank. mm10 dense full-genome gquantiles: hung, now ~75 s (multitask) / ~270 s (single-process).

title: misha 5.6.19
text: Fixed gintervals.load failing “invalid columns definition” gintervals.save bigset whose input character chrom (e.g. tibble dplyr). -disk per-chromosome files .meta zeroline now store chrom/chrom1/chrom2 factor full ALLGENOME levels, -disk frame normalized plain data.frame.

title: misha 5.6.18
text: Added gsynth.score(): writes misha fixed-bin dense track summed natural-log conditional probability trained stratified Markov-k model. Two scored tracks subtracted resolution give windowed log-Bayes-factor. mask argument NA-poisons positions inside mask (e.g. repeats); predicted-base N unconditional NA. gsynth.sample() now looks stratum bin pos - k match gsynth.train(). Previously queried bin predicted-base position, differed training first k bp every iter window. Cached .gsm models unchanged; samples generated earlier versions slight stratum-shift artifact iter boundaries. Added getOption("gmultitasking.strategy") gextract (default "auto"). large many-track workloads (>= 8 tracks, non-streaming iterator) auto routes track-parallel mode (worker handles track subset across tiles) instead legacy tile-parallel mode. Realistic 3,110 motif tracks x 2.19M peaks: 57.6 min vs ~3.4 h projected (3.5x per-track speedup). Override options(gmultitasking.strategy = "tracks" | "tiles" | "auto").

title: misha 5.6.17
text: Fixed gextract thousands tracks failing “many open files” (EMFILE). BufferedFile handles now released data loaded (sparse) mmapped (dense), open-FD count longer scales track count. Negligible perf cost. Fixed dense-track gextract regression introduced v5.6.11 calls ~50 motif tracks became 10-20x slower. MmapFile longer eagerly pages MAP_POPULATE, track-validation loops use metadata-path (stat size, read bin_size ) instead round-tripping init_read() per chromosome per track. Tamar’s 51-motif workload: 22 s -> 0.4 s. Added opt-performance regression test (MISHA_PERF_TESTS=true) covering many-track gextract setup overhead.

title: misha 5.6.16
text: gsynth.sample() output_format = "fasta" now writes samtools-compatible .fai alongside FASTA, removing need call samtools faidx hand. Matches convention already used ggenome.implant(). Added cell_merge argument gsynth.sample() companion exported utility gsynth.cell_merge(). Unlike bin_merge (redirects bins independently along dimension), cell_merge redirects specific per-joint-cell CDFs joint cells (e.g. (GC=0.725, CG=0.05) -> (GC=0.70, CG=0.08)). Intended reassigning -trained joint cells nearest-sufficient neighbor avoid sequence leakage tiny training sets. Added gsynth.forbid_kmer(model, pattern) returning new gsynth.model whose samples guaranteed pattern-free downstream seeding window (e.g. gsynth.forbid_kmer(model, "CG") CpG-null background). Pattern length capped model$k + 1.

title: misha 5.6.16
text: Fixed gsynth.sample() silently falling back uniform-random sampling positions inside interval whose start aligned model$iterator (#94). Output k-mer statistics unaligned intervals wrong; composition partially uniform.

title: misha 5.6.15
text: Fixed gsynth.train(), gsynth.sample(), gsynth.random_seqs() silently reading sequences wrong chromosome intervals omitted one earlier chromosomes chromkey - C++ side opened wrong sequence (shifted number earlier missing chromosomes), producing invalid models corrupted sampled genomes without error. Calls passed intervals = gintervals.() (left default) affected. Users ran functions custom interval subsets re-run version.

title: misha 5.6.14
text: Fixed indexed tracks re-mmapping entire track.dat every chromosome iterator init chromosome transitions. Made indexed tracks unusable genomes many contigs (e.g. Pan_troglodytes 4344 contigs).

title: misha 5.6.13
text: Fixed pwm.max.pos returning wrong strand sign. direction (positive/negative) returned position determined last scanned position interval rather position best score. Bug existed since pwm.max.pos introduced (v4.3.0).

title: misha 5.6.12
text: Fixed child processes surviving rexit() due R’s SIGTERM handler. multitasked operations (gmultitasking = TRUE) affected. Track-creating functions (gtrack.create, gtrack.smooth, gtrack.create_pwm_energy) corrupt data indexed databases children ran gtrack.convert_to_indexed concurrently. Non-indexed track data query functions (gextract, gscreen, gdist, gquantiles, …) unaffected (data written shared memory failed exit).

title: misha 5.6.11
text: Added ggenome.implant() replacing intervals reference genome donor sequences writing new FASTA. Supports literal donor sequences extraction misha database, optional trackdb creation. Added ggenome.transplant() sugar cross-genome sequence swaps - extracts source genome implants target genome single call.

title: misha 5.6.10
text: Fixed direction="" bidirect=TRUE taking min across strands instead max. genomic substitution changes strands, disrupting motif requires strands fall threshold. Breaking: removed hidden default set score.min = score.thresh direction = "". score.min now defaults NULL (filter) directions. Set score.min explicitly filter windows. Improved edit distance documentation: dedicated section direction/strand semantics, parameter reference, worked examples.

title: misha 5.6.9
text: Added k parameter gsynth.train() configure Markov order (1-8, default 5). 14-20x faster PWM scoring across code paths (gextract PWM vtracks, gseq.pwm, PWM edit distance). Replaced switch-statement DNA base encoding O(1) lookup tables inner scoring loop. Fixed typo DnaPSSM::integrate_energy (case 'h' case 'g') reverse-complement scoring path. affected function dead code (user-facing callers use integrate_energy_logspat), user-visible results affected.

title: misha 5.6.8
text: Added direction parameter (“”/“”) PWM edit distance functions computing minimum edits bring score threshold (motif disruption).

title: misha 5.6.7
text: Added PWM edit distance virtual track functions: pwm.edit_distance, pwm.edit_distance.pos, pwm.max.edit_distance, pwm.edit_distance.lse, pwm.edit_distance.lse.pos. Compute minimum edit distance (substitutions indels) reach PWM score threshold, per-window (max) aggregate (LSE) scoring modes. Added gseq.pwm_edits() retrieving detailed per-edit information (positions replacement bases) PWM edit distance computation. Enabled sub-chromosome range splitting gscreen gextract, improving parallel efficiency genomes large chromosomes. Fixed gscreen returning split intervals sub-chromosome parallel boundaries instead merged contiguous intervals. Enabled sub-chromosome range splitting gsummary, gdist, gcor (Pearson), improving parallel efficiency explicit iterators. Multiple performance improvements gscreen gextract dense iterators.

title: misha 5.6.3
text: Fixed gdataset.load() performance: loading large database dataset now fast regardless call order. Previously, gsetroot(small_db); gdataset.load(large_db) extremely slow dataset scan used R’s list.files(recursive=TRUE), lists every file tree. Replaced fast path reads .db.cache falls back C++ fts-based scanning. Also changed gdb.reload() calls gdataset.load()/gdataset.unload() use rescan=FALSE, existing databases use cache instead rescanned. Fixed collision detection hierarchical tracks gdataset.load(): R-level scan returned /-separated names dataset map uses .-separated names, causing collision detection silently fail tracks subdirectories.

Returns named lists position probability matrices directly usable gseq.pwm(). parsers native new dependencies. Added track export functions: gtrack.export_bedgraph() gtrack.export_bigwig() exporting tracks track expressions standard bedGraph BigWig formats. Supports gzip compression, virtual tracks, track expressions, custom iterators.

text: gsynth.save() gsynth.load() now use cross-platform .gsm format (YAML metadata + binary arrays) instead R-specific RDS. Models saved pymisha can now loaded R vice versa. title: misha 5.6.0
text: Added gintervals.attr.get(), gintervals.attr.set(), gintervals.attr.export(), gintervals.attr.import() managing interval set attributes. Attributes stored .iattr binary files (null-separated key/value pairs) next .interv files small interval sets, inside directory big interval sets. gintervals.rm() now cleans companion .iattr attribute files deleting interval sets.

title: misha 5.5.2
text: Replaced naive variance formula (E[X²]-E[X]²) Welford’s numerically stable online algorithm standard deviation computation track types (GenomeTrackFixedBin, GenomeTrackSparse, GenomeTrackInMemory, GenomeTrackArrays). naive formula prone catastrophic cancellation values large small variance relative mean. Improved sum accumulation precision using double-precision intermediate accumulators non-sliding sum paths. m_last_sum member remains float API compatibility, per-interval accumulation now happens double, eliminating float->float rounding errors large sums. Fixed potential --bounds access SAMPLE/SAMPLE_POS functions random number generator returns exactly 1.0. Added bounds clamping (ported pymisha). Fixed umask leak GenomeTrack::write_type() GenomeTrackFixedBin::init_write() - old umask now saved restored immediately open(), preventing permanent process-wide umask changes. Improved header validation GenomeTrackFixedBin::init_read() use integer modulo instead floating-point division, additional underflow guard. Added reusable scratch buffers (m_scratch_all_values, m_scratch_all_positions) GenomeTrackFixedBin, avoiding per-call heap allocation SAMPLE/SAMPLE_POS operations (ported pymisha).

title: misha 5.5.1
text: Fixed floating-point precision drift sliding window sum fixed-bin virtual tracks. incremental add/subtract pattern accumulated rounding errors (~1e-7 per step) compounded noticeable differences genome-wide scale. Now uses Kahan compensated summation bit-accurate results. bug introduced version 5.4.3 (commit 7337ff30, 2026-02-09) part fixed-bin sum optimization.

title: misha 5.5.0
text: Added indexed format support 2D tracks (rectangles points). Per-chromosome-pair files can now consolidated single track.dat + track.idx, matching indexed format already available 1D tracks. New function gtrack.2d.convert_to_indexed() converts existing 2D tracks indexed format optional removal old per-pair files. gtrack.convert_to_indexed() now dispatches 2D conversion automatically given rectangles points track. gdb.convert_to_indexed() convert_tracks = TRUE now includes 2D tracks batch conversion. 2D tracks created via gtrack.2d.create(), gtrack.2d.import(), gtrack.2d.import_contacts() automatically converted indexed format database indexed mode.

title: misha 5.4.8
text: Fixed NaN comparison bug distance.center virtual track iterator modifiers - used != instead std::isnan(), causing guard condition always true IEEE 754 semantics. Fixed distance virtual track returning NaN instead valid distance one side sorted interval array intervals current chromosome (NaN-unsafe min sequential path). Fixed gtrack.smooth MEAN algorithm producing spurious NaN values periodic recalculation NaN values present smoothing window. recalculation checked isnan accumulator instead incoming value, permanently poisoning sum. Fixed incorrect standard deviation/variance computation virtual tracks filter/mask - parallel variance formula used already-incremented weight instead pre-increment value. Fixed min.pos/max.pos virtual track aggregation comparing genomic positions instead signal values combining sub-intervals, returning leftmost/rightmost sub-interval position instead position actual min/max value. Fixed missing out_of_range check distance.center virtual track iterator modifiers, causing undefined behavior source intervals lie upstream query coordinate. Fixed copy-paste error quantile track computation highest_vals buffer resized using kid_lowest_vals_buf_size instead kid_highest_vals_buf_size. Fixed int32 truncation int64_t genomic coordinates gintervals.normalize - silently produce wrong results chromosomes longer ~2.1 Gbp. Fixed p-value transformation (pv function) skipped virtual track filter p-value function active. Fixed lse_accumulate double overload producing NaN inputs -infinity (missing isinf guards float overload ). Fixed GInterval::dist2coord treating coord == end inside interval, inconsistent half-open [start, end) convention used throughout codebase.

Use force=TRUE override (working db always wins) gdataset.load(): Load dataset namespace (tracks intervals become available) gdataset.unload(): Remove dataset namespace gdataset.save(): Create new dataset selected tracks/intervals gdataset.ls(): List working database loaded datasets gdataset.info(): Show metadata contents dataset gtrack.dataset(): Get source path track (working db dataset) gtrack.dbs(): Get paths track exists (debugging shadowed tracks) gintervals.dataset(): Get source path interval set gintervals.dbs(): Get paths interval set exists gtrack.ls(db = "/path//dataset"): List tracks specific source gintervals.ls(db = "/path//dataset"): List intervals specific source Cross-database operations: Track expressions work seamlessly tracks different sources datasets must identical chrom_sizes.txt files (genome assembly) Virtual tracks remain global (shared across loaded sources) Backward compatible: single database usage gsetroot() works unchanged gtrack.mv(): Rename move track within database gtrack.copy(): Copy track (can copy databases multiple loaded) Added gcor function computes correlation two tracks, multiple pairs tracks. title: misha 5.3.0
text: New indexed format (default): Uses unified genome.seq + genome.idx files instead per-chromosome files Dramatically reduces file descriptor usage genomes many contigs Provides 4-14% performance improvement large-scale analyses Removes requirement “chr” prefix chromosome names. Backward compatible: Legacy per-chromosome format fully supported Automatic format detection - user action required New functions: gdb.info(), gdb.convert_to_indexed(), gtrack.convert_to_indexed(), gintervals.convert_to_indexed(), gintervals.2d.convert_to_indexed() Set options(gmulticontig.indexed_format = FALSE) create databases legacy format compatibility older misha versions See vignette("Database-Formats") details. gmax.processes automatically set 70% available CPU cores gmax.data.size coordinated process limits ensure total memory usage <= 70% RAM (capped 10GB per process) Formula: gmax.data.size = min((RAM * 0.7) / gmax.processes, 10GB) ensures safe memory usage across parallel processes Dynamic auto-disable threshold: small datasets automatically use single-threaded mode avoid fork overhead Threshold scales system: gmax.processes * 1000 records (e.g., 2K laptops, 89K 128-core servers) Manual override still supported via options() See “Auto-Configuration” section vignette("Manual") details Added -memory value-based virtual tracks (gvtrack.create src parameter). tracks behave exactly like regular sparse tracks, stored memory can used track expressions. Added sshift, eshift filter parameters gvtrack.create. Added gintervals.path() gtrack.path() functions return actual file system paths interval sets tracks. Added masked.count masked.frac virtual track functions count fraction masked base pairs (lowercase letters) current iterator interval. Added distance.edge virtual track function computes edge--edge distance iterator interval closest source interval, using calculation gintervals.neighbors.

text: Added src_overlap_policy tgt_overlap_policy parameters gintervals.liftover, gintervals.load_chain, gtrack.liftover functions. Added target aggregation gtrack.liftover via multi_target_agg parameter. gintervals.load_chain now returns valid misha intervals instead chain object. gintervals.load_chain now includes score chain_id columns loaded chains New min_score parameter gintervals.load_chain, gintervals.liftover, gtrack.liftover filters low-quality chains New tgt_overlap_policy = "auto_score" ("auto") selects best chain mapping based alignment score (highest score -> longest span -> lowest chain_id) New include_metadata parameter gintervals.liftover optionally returns score chain_id mapping BREAKING: “auto” now alias “auto_score”. old behavior, use tgt_overlap_policy = "auto_first". Added canonic parameter gintervals.liftover (default FALSE) merge adjacent target intervals resulting source interval chain. tgt_overlap_policy = "best_cluster_union" (default, aliased "best_source_cluster"): Uses source union coverage tgt_overlap_policy = "best_cluster_sum": Uses sum target lengths tgt_overlap_policy = "best_cluster_max": Uses longest single member
